notes: type: card = text on black | clip = existing generated video (matched by filename substring in assets/clips) | still = image with slow push-in (assets/stills) | slate = placeholder for a shot that still has to be generated (shows its description). 'match' is matched case-insensitively against filenames. 'speed' < 1 slows a clip (frame-blended) to fill its slot; remaining time is held on the last frame. items.text:
WHAT WAS GIVEN ME

the Gospel of Mary, remembered

The first pages of Mary's gospel did not survive.

What follows is imagined.

items.desc: Dawn over flat-roofed first-century city, low haze, a woman's silhouette on a rooftop edge (Mary, late 40s, linen head-wrap).

vo.text: They say the first pages of my story are lost. Torn away, or turned to dust.
I do not mind. I remember them.

items.desc: Extreme close-up of Mary's weathered hands kneading dough on a rough wooden board, flour in morning light.

vo.text: I was not a queen, or a saint. I kept a house. I carried water. I was afraid, and I was grieved.

items.desc: Mary from behind walking a narrow whitewashed lane carrying a clay water jar on her shoulder, sunlit end of lane ahead.

vo.text: And every morning I walked to hear him speak.

items.desc: Macro: a single oil-lamp flame in a dark room, wick trembling, warm amber against deep black, fine film grain.

vo.text: He taught us that everything that is made is bound to everything else.

items.desc: Macro: a seed cupped in a weathered palm, then roots and soil; slow, tender, natural light.

vo.text: That nothing stands alone. That what is joined will, in time, return to its root.

items.desc: Wide, a courtyard at dusk; the Teacher (figure only, always backlit, face never resolved) speaks to seated listeners; Mary's POV from among them.

vo.text: He said the trouble is not out in the world. We make it, when we forget what we are joined to.
Be of good courage. Even when you are discouraged, take courage.

items.desc: Slow pan across listening faces in lamplight: Peter, Andrew, Levi, mouths closed, eyes lifted. Mary's POV.

vo.text: We sat together, all of us, in the upper room, and we listened.

items.match: weathered woman's hand resting on a rough wooden doorframe

vo.text: Now the morning comes back to me whole. The grain of the doorframe. The dust in the light.

items.match: Wide static shot inside a modest first-century upper room

vo.text: The men were frightened. I could hear it in how quietly they breathed.

items.match: Two-shot the Saviour stands at the room's open doorway

vo.text: Peace be with you. Receive my peace to yourselves. Beware that no one leads you astray, saying, 'Look, here,' or 'Look, there.'

items.match: Close on the Saviour, still softly backlit

vo.text: Go therefore and preach the good news of the kingdom. Lay down no rule beyond what I have set for you, and give no law like the lawgiver, lest you be bound by it.

items.match: gaze lowered, a single tear caught but not falling

vo.text: I did not know it was the last time I would hear his voice so near.

items.match: True point-of-view shot from Mary's eyes

vo.text: I saw him, standing in the light of the door. Exactly as he was.

items.match: the Saviour's silhouette turns and dissolves

vo.text: And then there was only light.

items.match: the disciples collapse into open grief

vo.text: How shall we go to the nations and preach the good news of the kingdom, if they did not spare him? How will they spare us?

items.match: Close on Andrew's frightened face
Mary rises from among the seated

vo.text: So I stood. Someone had to.

items.match: Medium shot Mary stands before the seated disciples

vo.text: Do not weep, and do not grieve, and do not doubt. His grace will be with you all and will shelter you. Let us praise his greatness, for he has prepared us and made us into men.

items.match: Close on Peter's face, mouth closed and still
Wide shot easing into a slow push toward Andrew

vo.text: How is it we never heard these words? He walked with us every day.

items.match: Slow push in on Mary's face, calm and composed

vo.text: I was afraid. I spoke anyway.

items.match: Two-shot Peter turns to Mary

vo.text: Sister, we know that the Saviour loved you more than the rest of women. Tell us the words of the Saviour which you remember, which you know but we do not, nor have we heard them.

items.match: Close on Mary as she answers Peter

vo.text: What is hidden from you, I will proclaim to you.

items.match: her eyes going distant as she remembers

vo.text: I saw the Lord in a vision, and I said to him: Lord, I saw you today in a vision. And he answered and said to me: Blessed are you, that you did not waver at the sight of me. For where the mind is, there is the treasure.

items.match: Abstract transition the upper room's window light shifts
a single small point of soft light rises

vo.text: The soul answered and said: what binds me has been overcome, and my desire has ended, and ignorance has died.

items.match: a thick wall of pure darkness presses inward

vo.text: The first power was Darkness.

items.match: warm restless flickering light, like candle flame multiplied

vo.text: The second was Desire.

items.match: dense grey fog rolls across frame

vo.text: The third was Ignorance.

items.desc: ABSTRACT, no figures/faces: seven distinct bands of harsh reddish light flare and layer across frame in rapid overlapping succession; the point of light holds steady.

vo.text: These are the seven powers of wrath. And they asked the soul: Where do you come from, killer of men? Where are you going, conqueror of space?

items.desc: ABSTRACT: all light and shadow settle into a single soft steady glow, calm, unmoving, filling the frame. Pure visual silence.

vo.text: From this time on I will attain rest, for the time, for the season, for the age, in silence.

items.match: Extreme close-up on Mary's face, eyes glistening but composed

vo.text: Then I was quiet. The room was quiet. And I waited to be answered.

items.match: Close on Andrew, uneasy, turning to the other men

vo.text: Say what you wish to say about what she has told us, but I do not believe that the Saviour said this. For these teachings are strange ideas.

items.match: lips closed and unmoving throughout, her gaze drifting away

vo.text: It was the first cut. It is strange, how small a voice can wound.

items.desc: Wide: Peter rises, agitated, turning the room's doubt into open accusation against Mary; the other men shift uneasily around him.

vo.text: Did he really speak privately with a woman and not openly to us? Are we to turn around and all listen to her? Did he prefer her to us?

items.desc: Close on Mary, tears finally breaking through her composure, hurt but not backing down; mouth closed.

vo.text: My brother Peter, what do you think? Do you think that I thought this up myself in my heart, or that I am lying about the Saviour?

items.desc: Wide: the whole room frozen in the aftermath. Mary weeping but upright, Peter standing, Andrew looking away in shame, Levi watching from where he sits apart.
Medium: Levi rises from where he sat apart and calm, moving to the centre of the room with quiet deliberate authority.
Two-shot easing into a slow low push-in on Levi confronting Peter, calm but unyielding; other disciples behind him fall out of focus.

vo.text: Peter, you have always been hot-tempered. Now I see you contending against this woman like the adversaries. But if the Saviour made her worthy, who are you to reject her? Surely the Saviour knew her very well.

items.desc: Close on Peter, the fight draining out of him, looking down, chastened by Levi's words.
Close on Levi turning to address the whole group, calling them back to their purpose.

vo.text: Rather, let us be ashamed, and put on the perfect man, and acquire him for ourselves as he commanded us, and preach the good news, laying down no other rule or law beyond what the Saviour said.

items.match: composed again, a small grateful glance toward Levi

vo.text: I did not need to be believed by all of them. I only needed one to remember what he had said.

items.match: the disciples rise together from around the low table
Mary pausing at the doorway threshold

vo.text: I looked back once. The room was empty, and it was not.

items.match: Wide shot from behind a small group of first-century disciples

vo.text: And they began to go out, to proclaim and to preach.

items.match: slow push toward Mary's face, at peace

vo.text: This is what he gave me. Not a title. Not their belief. Only what I saw, and the courage to say it.

items.text:
The Gospel of Mary survives in a single Coptic manuscript
of the 5th century (Papyrus Berolinensis 8502).
Several of its pages are lost.
